findings.explanation: The SPL has no rollup and returns every transfer_to_gen, retransfer_to_utility or test event regardless of duration, in addition to any with duration_ms above 500.
findings.quote: Rolls up `count` by `entity` across `the scheduled window` and pages when `duration_ms` > 500.
findings.suggested_fix: State that every generator transfer, retransfer and test event is listed, and that transfers longer than 500 ms are also listed.

findings.explanation: The sentence refers to an unnamed field in props and to the App field (`described in App`) instead of naming the field and the ATS MIB or relay source.
findings.quote: the relay or trap source field referenced in props
findings.suggested_fix: Name the trap or relay field and give an example event.

findings.explanation: Neither this path nor `Data/ManagingSNMPdata` is known to be a current Splunk Enterprise documentation page; the SNMP page I know is titled Send SNMP events to your Splunk deployment.
findings.suggested_fix: Open both URLs and replace any that do not resolve.

findings.explanation: The scenarios are template wording. The SPL pages on test events, so every scheduled generator exercise or ATS test is a false positive, and none of this is mentioned.
findings.quote: Scheduled automation elevates `src` without crossing `duration_ms` > 500 for UC-15.1.13.
findings.suggested_fix: List scheduled exercise and test transfers, momentary utility sags causing short transfers, and planned maintenance bypass.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: Alerting on every event IN (transfer_to_gen, retransfer_to_utility, test) means routine scheduled tests page operators; the 500 ms threshold has no stated basis in ATS specifications.

summary: The data model for ATS events is described well, but the description says the alert depends on duration_ms while the SPL fires on every transfer or test event. References contain doc paths that need checking.
